conceptBreakdown.title: Allergic Hypersensitivity Cascade & Autoimmune Pathologies

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Allergies are exaggerated Type I hypersensitivity responses driven by IgE binding to mast cells, releasing histamine and serotonin. Treatment utilizes antihistamines, epinephrine, and corticosteroids. Autoimmunity arises when immunological self-tolerance fails, causing auto-antibodies and autoreactive T-cells to destroy self-tissues.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ALLERGIC HYPERSENSITIVITY CASCADE
                         
   First Exposure to Allergen ──► B-cells produce excess IgE Antibodies
                                             │
   IgE binds Fc receptors on Mast Cells and Basophils
                                             │
   Re-exposure to Allergen ──► Allergen cross-links IgE ──► Mast Cell Degranulation
                                             │
   Releases Vasoactive Amines: Histamine and Serotonin
                                             │
   Symptoms: Vasodilation, broncho-spasm, watery eyes, running nose, Anaphylaxis
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 6.1 Allergic Hypersensitivity (Type I Reaction)
- **Allergen**: Non-pathogenic environmental antigens (e.g., pollen grains, dust mites, pet dander, penicillin, bee venom).
- **Molecular Mechanism**:
  1. **Sensitization Phase**: Initial exposure to allergen induces class-switching in B-lymphocytes to produce high levels of **$\text{IgE}$ antibodies**.
  2. **Effector Phase**: $\text{IgE}$ binds firmly via its constant region to high-affinity $\text{Fc}\epsilon\text{RI}$ receptors on tissue **Mast Cells** and circulating **Basophils**.
  3. **Degranulation**: Subsequent re-exposure to the allergen causes allergen molecules to cross-link adjacent membrane-bound $\text{IgE}$ molecules, triggering explosive exocytosis (degranulation) of pre-formed basophilic granules.
  4. **Chemical Mediators**: Releases **Histamine**, **Serotonin**, leukotrienes, and prostaglandins.
  5. **Clinical Manifestations**: Peripheral vasodilation, increased capillary permeability (edema), broncho-constriction (asthma), watery eyes, sneezing, and systemic **Anaphylactic Shock** (life-threatening collapse in blood pressure).
- **Pharmacological Intervention**: **Antihistamines**, **Adrenaline (Epinephrine)**, and **Corticosteroids** rapidly reverse bronchospasm and hypotension.

### 6.2 Autoimmune Diseases (Loss of Self-Tolerance)

```
                        KEY AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES
                        
   1. RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS ──► Auto-antibodies (Rheumatoid Factor - IgM) attack synovial membranes.
   2. MYASTHENIA GRAVIS   ──► Auto-antibodies block Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptors at NMJ.
   3. TYPE 1 DIABETES     ──► Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic β-cells.
   4. HASHIMOTO'S DISEASE ──► Auto-antibodies destroy thyroid follicular cells ("Thyroid Suicide").
   5. MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS   ──► Autoimmune destruction of CNS myelin sheaths.
```

conceptBreakdown.heading: Central vs Peripheral Tolerance
conceptBreakdown.title: Central vs Peripheral Tolerance

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Central tolerance in thymus (AIRE-mediated negative selection) and bone marrow eliminates autoreactive immature lymphocytes; peripheral tolerance (Anergy, Treg suppression) silences escaped autoreactive cells.

conceptBreakdown.content: Central tolerance in the thymus eliminates autoreactive T-cell clones through negative selection mediated by the AIRE (Autoimmune Regulator) transcription factor; breakdown in central or peripheral regulatory T-cell (Treg) suppression triggers clinical autoimmune diseases.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Hygiene Hypothesis
conceptBreakdown.title: Hygiene Hypothesis
conceptBreakdown.content: The hygiene hypothesis suggests that modern sterile environments and reduced childhood exposure to diverse microbes skew immune development toward Th2 responses, increasing the prevalence of asthma and atopic allergies.
